feedback: Iteration 0 (the symmetric 0.04 m array, wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8, kp 3.0, base_speed 1.4) raced 60 trials with 0 finishes and 100 percent off-track exits. Progress stalled at 0.075 to 0.15 and max_error was 0.060 to 0.069 m, at or just above the 0.06 m floor, with 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. The evidence points to the robot losing the line on bends, not to speed, because runs ended long before the 3 s limit mattered. I did not have to compensate for speed-related behaviour; I did reduce kp and raise kd in the controller to cope with the narrower wheel_track you asked for, so the geometry is effectively more responsive per unit of PWM. Before the next race, use these rules: if the new run still ends off-track with max_error above 0.05 m and line_loss_events of 1 or more, widen the array further (for example x = -0.04 to +0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing) before changing wheel_track again. If the run completes but completion_time is above about 3 s, that is the first evidence that speed is limiting, and then raise wheel_radius toward 0.035 m. If steering_oscillation is high (above about 0.2) while max_error is low, reduce the sensor weights to [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1] rather than changing the sensor positions.
requested_changes: If off-track exits persist with max_error above 0.05 m after the wider array, widen the sensor span to x = -0.04 to +0.04 m (five sensors at 0.02 m spacing); iteration 0 showed a 0.06 m max_error and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run, so more span is the direct lever.
Do not raise wheel_radius yet: no iteration 0 run completed, so the speed-limit evidence is absent. Only raise wheel_radius to 0.035 m if a future race completes with completion_time above about 3 s.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with max_error low, lower the sensor weights to [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1] before changing the geometry, since iteration 0 oscillation was 0.13 to 0.17 and the Integrator reduced kp rather than adding gain.
